title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 129
paragraphs: So he was discovered in this manner. Three months had gone by while Artabazos was besieging the town, when there came a great, long-lasting ebb of the sea; and the barbarians, seeing the shallow water, tried to cross into the peninsula of Pallene. When, however, they had passed through two-fifths of the distance, with three-fifths still remaining before they would be inside Pallene, a great flood-tide came upon them, higher than ever before — as the natives of the place say, though high tides come often. Those who could not swim perished, and those who could were killed by the men of Potidaia, who put out to them in boats. The cause of the high tide and flood and of what befell the Persians was this, as the Potidaians say: these same Persians who perished in the sea had committed impiety against the temple of Poseidon and his image in the suburb of the town. In saying this was the cause, in my opinion they say well. The survivors of his army Artabazos led away to Thessaly to join Mardonius. Thus fared those who escorted the king on his way.
